name: qwen3_0p6b
description: Qwen3 0.6B, the model this fabric is sized to host. Chosen because it is the largest of the candidates whose int8 weights fit the 1 GB DDR3L on a Zybo Z7-20 (596 MB), and it is the model Architect Labs demonstrated hosting locally.
notes: Qwen3-0.6B: 28 layers, hidden 1024, intermediate 3072, 16 query heads over 8 key/value heads (grouped query attention).
int8 weights are 596 MB, which fits the Zybo Z7-20's 1 GB DDR3L. The next size up, TinyLlama 1.1B, does not.

Batch-1 decode reads every weight once per token, so a single board at 2 GB/s sustained is bounded near 3.4 tokens/s and two boards splitting the weights near 7. That bound is memory bandwidth, not arithmetic: the MAC chiplet is idle most of the time and adding more of them does not help.
d_ff 3072 is the longest reduction, so it sets the accumulator width the same way it did for GPT-2; the derived hardware is identical in shape and different in size.
Megatron tensor parallelism: QKV and c_fc column-parallel, out-proj and c_proj row-parallel.

Batch-1 decode identity: every block weight is used exactly once per token, so per-token block MACs equal block parameter count, and weight traffic per token equals per_token_macs * weight_bits / 8 bytes. The LM head and embeddings are excluded from both compute and traffic (modeled as host-side).
